references.sentence: System Overview The WPG of this paper is part of a two-chip solution for DVD and CD writing and rewriting, as can be seen from Fig. 1.

The two most important advantages of this two-chip solution compared to a single-chip laser driver located on the pickup head are lower heat generated on the pickup head, where heat is difﬁcult to dissipate, and fewer connections over the ﬂexible PCB (5 signal lines only, compared to 14 signal lines to and from the processor; see Fig. 1).
Fig. 1.
As is already seen in Fig. 1, the processor sends the data “DATAIN P/N” to be written to the CD or DVD along with a clock signal “CLK”.
Output Current Stage The output of the write pulse generator chip is connected to the laser driver chip across several centimeters of a ﬂexible printed circuit board, as can be seen in Fig. 1.
The six levels of the laser current are labeled “e” (erase), “fw” (ﬁrst write), Fig. 2. “b” (bottom), “mp” (multi-pulse), “lw” (last write), “c” (cool).
As an example, the laser current waveform together with the corresponding WPG output current are depicted in Fig. 2 for a typical DVD-RAM write strategy.

Typical HD-DVD strategies are very similar to the DVD-RAM strategy shown in Fig. 2, but the number of multi-pulses is higher by 1, e.g., a 7 T mark has 4 instead of 3 multi-pulses and the shortest allowed mark length is 2 T.
This latency is not shown in Fig. 2.
Other standards than DVD-RAM use simpliﬁed variants of the patterns shown in Fig. 2.
The idea of shunting a pair of inverters at the output has already been proposed (though not implemented) in 1993 [9], Fig. 2.
